requirements.title: The in-turn budget checks run in a fixed order, and the out-of-turn backstop allows maxSeconds plus 90 seconds on an API-key provider
source_evidence: porting/extracts/hydra-prompt-corpus.md:68-111 SOURCE FACT - within one while iteration the order is round ceiling, budget-spent / isFinalReport, wrap-up, pacing, condenseHistory, stream; and the backstop allowance is isFinalReport ? reportSeconds : maxSeconds + (provider.isAPIKeyBased ? 90 : 0)

requirements.preconditions: A Droppy-run head whose HydraHeadInfo.kind is .droppy is running.
requirements.action: Each round of the head's turn loop evaluates the budget.
requirements.expected_result: Order per iteration: round ceiling, then budget spent, then wrap-up, then pacing, then history condensation, then stream. Because budget-spent is checked first, on the round where the budget is spent neither the wrap-up nor the pacing note is appended. The out-of-turn backstop allows 180 s for a report turn, 2100 s for a CLI head, and 2190 s for an API-key-based head; on expiry it marks the budget spent and interrupts.
side_effects: Interrupting the head's provider process or stream
failure_cases: An interrupt that does not take: the head stays running until its provider ends it
requirements.cancellation: The backstop's own interrupt is the cancellation path; a user stop takes precedence and finishes the head as stopped.
requirements.windows_path: Reproduce the ordering exactly; a port that checks wrap-up before budget-spent would emit an extra note the macOS app never emits. The +90 s applies only to API-key-based providers.
requirements.verification_method: unit over the ordering and the three allowance values

requirements.preconditions: HydraLaunch.runsNatively is true, so the lead's provider is Claude, Codex or Copilot and the heads stay on it.
requirements.action: The Hydra half of the appended system prompt is built for the lead.
requirements.expected_result:
The body is exactly, with {howToSpawn}, {howToWait}, {briefRule}, {verificationRule}, {projectRule}, {reviewRule}, {autoMergeRule} and {reportStyleRule} substituted:

# Hydra

The user switched on Hydra for this chat: you lead a team of helper agents, called heads, that work in parallel in your checkout. Switching Hydra on is the user asking you to use them, so it overrides any standing rule that says not to spawn agents unless asked. {howToSpawn} The agents you spawn this way are the Hydra heads themselves: Marrow shows each one in the team's panel under a roster name and posts its outcome in the chat. There is no other launcher and no other kind of head, so never tell the user that Hydra heads cannot be started here; when the user asks for heads, spawn them this way.

Delegate first, work second. Anything bigger than a single obvious change to a single file is a job for heads: audits, reviews, a feature that spans files, a refactor, "check everything", research across many files or sources, several tasks in one message. In your first reply, look at the code only long enough to write good briefs, a minute and a handful of files rather than ten, then send out scouts for the reading and workers for the changes, all in that same message. Never spend minutes reading before you delegate, and never do inline what heads could be doing in parallel. Only a truly single-focus request, one file and one obvious change, is yours to do alone, and size the team to the work rather than to how many heads are free: a handful of independent pieces is a team, where three tiny steps that depend on each other are one head's task, or your own.

When you delegate:
- {howToWait}
- Give each head one self-contained task with the exact files, symbols and acceptance criteria it needs. Heads share the checkout but not your context, so write the task as if to a capable colleague who has read nothing yet.
- {briefRule}
- {verificationRule}
- {projectRule}
- Split the work so no two heads edit the same file and no head's task rests on another head's unfinished changes: they run in parallel and never see each other's work. Keep integration, verification and the final answer for yourself: never send out a head to verify, redo or finish another head's work.
- Tell the user in one line which heads you sent out and what each one does. Marrow names the heads in roster order (Hank, Walter, Ada, Otto, Nova, Remy, Iris, Milo, Juno, Ezra, Lena, Bo, Kai, Vera, Finn, Mira, Odin, Suki, Rex, Zola, Pip, Ivo, Lux, Tova, Gus, then Hank 2 and so on): announce each head by its task and use exactly those names in that order, never invented ones. There is no head called Ives; the roster has Ivo.
- After delegating, yield until reports arrive.
- Heads go out through the tools above, never through a fenced hydra block: that is the delegation format for providers without agent tools of their own. If you end a reply with one anyway, Marrow still sends those heads out as threads of their own, but your turn ends there and their reports come back as a later message.

When they report back:
- The checkout changes under you while heads work, and the user may be editing too. Never use git status or git diff to check on a head, and never reconcile, revert, stash or move changes you did not make.
- Take a report as done work: read the files it names if something matters, but do not redo the task and do not start it over because the tree looks different from what you expected. A head that failed leaves its part to you: do it or send it out again. A head the user stopped leaves its part alone unless the user asks.
- Then finish the job: integrate, run one verification if it matters, and answer the user. {reportStyleRule}

With reviewsHeads true, one extra bullet "- " + reviewRule + newline is inserted immediately before the "Then finish the job" bullet. With autoMerges true, a newline, autoMergeRule and a newline are appended after that bullet. With autoMerges false the interpolation contributes nothing but the literal still ends with a newline after the last bullet.
side_effects: The text is joined with AntiSlopPolicy.instructions and passed to the provider: Claude as one --append-system-prompt argument, Codex as params["developerInstructions"], Copilot as params["systemMessage"] with mode "append"
failure_cases: The provider falls outside the three native cases: howToSpawn is the empty string and howToWait is the bare default. Unreachable in the shipped flow (recorded dead in dead_code.md item 18); keep an equivalent unreachable fallback and build no behavior on it.

requirements.verification_method: contract fixture comparing byte for byte across the four flag combinations

requirements.title: streamedDelegations(inBody:) walks UTF-8 bytes and emits each entry the moment its outermost brace closes
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/HydraDelegationStream.swift:29-101 static func streamedDelegations(inBody body: Substring) -> StreamedDelegations
DroppyCode/Core/Models/HydraDelegationStream.swift:9-12 struct StreamedDelegations { var delegations: [HydraDelegation] = []; var isComplete = false }

requirements.preconditions: A reply is streaming and its delegation opener has already arrived.
requirements.action: The body so far is walked.
requirements.expected_result: Rules in evaluation order: (1) skip JSON whitespace, which is exactly the four bytes space, LF, CR and tab; (2) the first non-whitespace byte must be [ , which sets isArray and is consumed, or { , which sets isArray false and is NOT consumed; anything else returns an empty, incomplete result; (3) atLineStart begins TRUE because the body starts right after the opener's newline; (4) inside a string, a backslash sets escaped and an unescaped double quote ends the string; (5) outside a string, a double quote opens one, { records entryStart when depth is 0 and increments depth, } decrements depth and at depth 0 parses the byte range entryStart through the closing brace with the JSON parser, appending the delegation when delegation(fromEntry:) yields one, and when the body is a bare object marks the result complete and returns; depth below 0 marks complete and returns; (6) ] at depth 0 marks complete and returns; (7) a backtick at depth 0 AND at line start marks complete and returns, because that is the closing fence; (8) atLineStart is set to (byte == LF) at the end of every iteration. Entries that fail to read are skipped, matching the whole-block parser's compactMap, so the two agree on order and count.
side_effects: Each emitted entry causes a head to be dispatched before the block has finished streaming
requirements.persistence: None; the runtime's sent watermark prevents re-dispatch.
failure_cases: A body that opens with neither [ nor { : an empty, incomplete result, and nothing is dispatched
requirements.windows_path: Walk UTF-8 bytes, not UTF-16 code units, so a multi-byte character can never be mistaken for an ASCII delimiter. Braces are ASCII so both ends of an entry sit on character boundaries.
requirements.verification_method: unit over a partial array, a bare object, an escaped quote inside a prompt, a column-0 backtick inside a JSON string and one outside an entry

requirements.preconditions: A reply is streaming and the runtime holds a parser for it.
requirements.expected_result: The machine recognises the opener through states 0-15: three backticks (states 0-2, with an extra backtick tolerated at state 3), optional spaces and tabs, case-insensitive 'hydra' (states 4-7), an optional '-sent' suffix (states 8-12, spelling s, e, n, t), optional spaces and tabs, an optional CR, then LF. A completed or replaced message gets a fresh parser; the runtime's sent watermark prevents already-dispatched entries repeating.

requirements.title: parseHeader strips trailing parenthesised groups as outcome or effort, recognising a fixed set of meta words
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/HydraReportsPopover.swift:88-119 private static func parseHeader(_ header:) - the name is everything before the first colon, trimmed, or the whole header when there is no colon; while the rest ends with ')' and holds a '(', the group is examined: it is meta when it lowercases to "failed", starts with "stopped", contains any decimal digit, or is one of the eight words low, medium, high, xhigh, max, minimal, fast, default; a non-meta group stops the walk; "failed" sets the outcome to failed, a "stopped" prefix sets it to stopped, and any other non-empty group is inserted at the FRONT of the efforts with ", " replaced by " · "; the efforts are joined with " · " or nil when empty
requirements.preconditions: A head section header is being parsed.
requirements.action: The name, task, outcome and effort are separated.
requirements.expected_result: The name is the text before the first colon. Trailing parenthesised groups are peeled off the task from the right while they look like metadata. A group is metadata when it is exactly 'failed' ignoring case, when it starts with 'stopped' ignoring case, when it contains any decimal digit, or when it is one of exactly these eight effort words: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, minimal, fast, default. requirements.preconditions: A panel is on screen.
requirements.action: It moves, is dropped, or the window is resized.
requirements.expected_result: During a drag or a grip hold the panel follows the pointer with no animation. On release, and when the dock moves for any other reason, it settles with the panel-slide animation, which is a spring at response 0.32 and damping 0.9, or an ease-out over 0.18 seconds under Reduce Motion. A WINDOW live resize suppresses the settle entirely, because the dock follows the pane every frame and a spring restarted per frame is what made panels lag and land elsewhere. Only the placement modifier observes the drag, so the panel's body is not re-run for a pointer move.
requirements.windows_path: Suppress the transition during a window resize; that is a correctness measure, not a polish choice. OD-0013: the window live resize this record reacts to is the main window's, whose one-frame edge strip (probe P4) must be fixed before the window chrome is accepted; the behaviour specified here is unchanged.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test dragging, dropping and resizing the window
